julia_acme: Hey, hitting 400 on /v1/rerank from our integration. We send a list of candidates but get 'empty candidates' error. request-id: req_9f3b2a

ana_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact request body and headers (curl) so we can repro?

julia_acme: Sure, here's what our integration emitted (redacted):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' \
  -d '{"items":"doc1,doc2,doc3","query":"best laptop","top_k":null}'
```

julia_acme: Response was HTTP 400 with body: `{"error":"invalid_request","message":"items must be a non-empty array","request_id":"req_9f3b2a"}`

ana_support: ah ok thanks. two red flags: Content-Type is text/plain and items is a single comma-separated string, not a JSON array. That will parse as a string server-side and fail validation.

raman_eng: Repro'd locally by sending items as a string. Server validation expects array of objects or strings. With text/plain the body gets handled as raw string and our JSON parser fails to coerce. Adding repro steps:

```bash
# reproducer
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' -d '{"items":"a,b,c","query":"q"}' -D -

# response snip
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"invalid_request","message":"items must be a non-empty array","request_id":"req_9f3b2a"}
```

raman_eng: SDKs sometimes accidentally stringify the payload when Content-Type mismatches. Which SDK/version are you using?

julia_acme: We're on internal node wrapper that calls fetch; we traced it to body = JSON.stringify(req.items.join(',')) so yep we turned array into comma string. Using node 18 and our wrapper v0.9.

ana_support: Action items: 1) for you: change to Content-Type: application/json and send items as an actual array: `{"items":["doc1","doc2","doc3"],"query":"best laptop","top_k":5}`. 2) for us: add a clearer error hint when body is valid JSON but items is wrong type, and add a FAQ note about common client bug (stringified arrays).

raman_eng: I will open an internal ticket to add a linter rule in the Node wrapper to prevent stringify-once-more bug and add server-side validation message: if typeof items === 'string' respond with code 400 and message 'items must be JSON array, got string (looks like comma-separated list)'. Also suggest including request-id in all 4xx responses (we already do but we'll ensure it's present).

ana_support: Also sending customer a quick-hotfix snippet: 
```js
// correct payload
const body = { items: ["doc1","doc2","doc3"], query: "best laptop", top_k: 5 }
fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Authorization: `Bearer ${KEY}` }, body: JSON.stringify(body) })
```

julia_acme: Thanks! Quick question — why did top_k=null cause anything? We sometimes set null when we want default behavior.

raman_eng: null is fine on our end; the main failure here was items being a string. top_k=null shouldn't break validation unless other fields are wrong type too.

ana_support: Marking this thread for follow-up: escalate to eng-runtime for a small validation patch and send customer remediation steps. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: PATCH eng-runtime 2026-04-03 02:30 UTC (validation message tweak).

julia_acme: Verified after we fixed our wrapper and set Content-Type: application/json — rerank returns 200 and scores look good. Thanks all! :tada:
